transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

A lazy yellow flame that leaves black soot usually means the gas isn't mixing properly with air at that burner. This is most often a simple issue: the burner cap (the removable metal disc) may be slightly out of position, blocked by food debris or grease, or wet from cleaning. When this happens, the gas flow is disrupted and combustion becomes incomplete. Please do the following owner-safe check:
1. Switch off the hob and ensure it is cool.
2. Lift off the burner cap and crown (the central part) for that back burner.
3. Check for any blockages in the small holes around the edge of the cap or in the base. Clean them gently with a dry cloth or soft brush if needed, ensuring everything is completely dry.
4. Re-seat the cap so it sits perfectly flat and square.
5. Try lighting that burner again. If the flame returns to a crisp blue and the soot stops, that was the cause. If the yellow flame persists even with a clean, correctly seated cap, this points to an issue with the gas pressure or air-mix adjustment at that specific burner outlet, which requires a Gas Safe engineer to adjust safely.
[Safety panel] If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.

I had a look at the burner cap and it seems to be seated properly, though there are some burnt spills around it. Your safety note made me remember that I've noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. Should I be worried about that?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Burner cap/crown misaligned, blocked, or dirty (high)
Incorrect gas pressure or air-mix adjustment (gas supply issue) (medium)

plan: They asked: "What's wrong with it?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "back burner flame is lazy yellow and leaves black soot on the pan". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
